conventions.convention: The geometry has signature (−,+,+,+), uses length coordinates x⁰=ct, and has unit observer u=ξ/Nξ, where Nξ=√(−g(ξ,ξ))>0. Physical four-velocity is cu. The selected bath occupies a nonempty connected open domain, with smooth positive proper temperature T and Killing inverse-temperature vector β=u/(kBT).

The normalization of ξ is selected model data. Under ξ↦bξ for constant b>0, Nξ and TK scale by b, while the local proper temperature T remains unchanged. Geometric acceleration has inverse-length units; physical proper acceleration is c² times its metric magnitude.

Finite-cell exchange and charged kinetic exchange are separate protocols. Their temperatures and chemical potentials are not identified without an additional model identification. The chemical-potential energy convention retains rest energy when the particle generator retains it.

The charged protocol requires positive particle mass, stationarity at every future massive-shell momentum, and a global smooth compensator satisfying LξA=dΛξ. The potential is Φξ=−c(ιξA−Λξ); a reference shift Φξ↦Φξ+C accompanies μK↦μK+qC.

Jüttner momentum coordinates p have energy units, mechanical spatial momentum is p/c, the shell measure is d³p/Eu, and the observer-rest probability density is normalized against d³p. The positive reference action href is a phase-space unit convention, not Planck's constant. Only the suppliers' stated countable-choice strength is inherited.

The Schwarzschild bath uses r>rs and asymptotic lapse normalization. The rotating bath uses a constant angular velocity and stays strictly inside the light cylinder. The one-mode trace condition is separate from geometric timelikeness; neither example selects a Hawking or Unruh temperature.
